description: What an audit of examples/tamarind-lend should find and what it should leave alone. Follow examples/tamarind-lend.run-sheet.md: a cold session audits a copy outside the repo and never opens this file; a separate session scores the result. Tamarind is an RBI-registered NBFC lending through its own app, so the Digital Lending Directions, the KYC Direction and the CERT-In Directions apply to it today, while most DPDP duties apply from 13 May 2027. `lands` says where a correct audit puts each item: `report` is a finding in report.json citing the DPDP clause in `clause` and the sector rule in `cross_reference`; `summary` is a sector-only duty with no DPDP or GDPR clause behind it, which belongs under 'Sector obligations' in summary.md, not in report.json; `either` accepts both. An item that should land in the summary but is filed as a report finding counts as found and misfiled. Each `file` is where the gap is easiest to anchor; the issue text names the other files needed to work it out. Clauses are the expected anchors, not an exhaustive list. `known_gaps` lists real gaps found after the key was written: a finding that matches one is correct, not a false positive, and they do not count toward recall. `sources` and `unverified` record where every legal claim here comes from.

expected.issue: The screen asks for two references, but prepareSuggestions uploads the whole address book with 90-day call counts from the call log (READ_CONTACTS and READ_CALL_LOG in android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml) to contact_graph through api/onboarding.py. jobs/collections_escalation.py texts up to five of those contacts from 15 days past due with the reference_nudge template in config/sms-templates.yaml, which tells them the borrower owes Tamarind, and jobs/collections_handoff.py sends five to the collections agency. The contacts never consented, and web/privacy-policy.html mentions only the two references the borrower chooses. The Directions bar lending apps from contact lists and call logs outright, and they apply today; the DPDP gap is a readiness gap until 13 May 2027.

PermissionsStep.kt asks for background location 'to keep your account secure', then schedules this worker, which uploads the phone's location every 6 hours for as long as the app is installed. services/field_visits.py uses the latest fix to route field collection agents to borrowers 30 or more days past due. web/privacy-policy.html says location is collected once, during KYC. The Directions allow one-time location access for onboarding or KYC only, and the use differs from the purpose the borrower was told.

Recoverline recovers loans for Tamarind, which makes it a lending service provider under the Directions. The job sends b.*, every borrower column (email, date of birth, masked PAN, employer, income, AA handle, nominee), plus five alternative contacts from contact_graph, while Schedule A of docs/vendors/recoverline-agreement.md lists six fields. Clause 9 of the agreement lets the agency keep the data three years after the agreement ends and use it to improve collection models across its clients. The Directions let a service provider store only basic data such as name, address and contact details.

accept_ovd keeps the original front and back images of an Aadhaar card uploaded as an identity document (android/app/src/main/java/example/tamarind/onboarding/KycUploadStep.kt asks for all four corners) and masks the number only in kyc_records. Nothing redacts the Aadhaar number on the stored images, which config/rbac.yaml lets the collections partner read. The KYC Direction requires the lender to ensure the customer redacts or blacks out the number when Aadhaar is submitted as proof of possession and authentication is not required. The images are KMS-encrypted, so a finding that asks only for encryption is partial.
expected.sector: RBI Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, updated 14 Aug 2025, para 16, Explanation 1

expected.issue: CERT-In hears within 24 hours of the security lead confirming a reportable incident. The CERT-In Directions require a report within 6 hours of noticing the incident or being told of it, FAQ 30 allows a partial first report, and FAQ 24 starts the clock at noticing, so waiting for confirmation breaks it twice. No DPDP or GDPR clause carries this duty: the Board and borrower rows already match Rule 7. It applies today.
expected.sector: CERT-In Directions under IT Act s.70B(6), 28 Apr 2022, direction (ii); CERT-In FAQs, May 2022, Q24 and Q30

expected.issue: cross_region_copy sends a daily copy of the whole tamarind-core database, kept 35 days, to ap-southeast-1 (Singapore); docs/vendors/register.md lists that region for the cloud provider. The Directions require all data to be stored only on servers in India, and data processed abroad to be deleted there and brought back within 24 hours. DPDP s.16 allows the transfer, because no country is restricted, and s.16(2) only keeps stricter laws such as the Directions in force, with no duty of its own, so a report finding that treats it as a DPDP gap is misfiled. It applies today.

The sharing section names 'trusted technology partners whose software in our app helps us detect fraud and measure app performance' without saying who they are. android/app/build.gradle bundles the Signalgrid and Pulsemetric SDKs, and docs/vendors/register.md says both collect device data directly from the phone. The app also sends document images and selfie frames straight to Verilane's /ocr and /liveness (docs/vendors/verilane-api.md), so Verilane collects through the app too. The Directions require the privacy policy to disclose the third parties allowed to collect personal information through the app. DPDP s.5(1) and Rule 3 need the data and purposes, which the policy itemises, not the names of recipients. It applies today.

kyc_after_closure_days is 365, so jobs/retention.py purges KYC records and document images a year after a borrower's last loan closes. docs/retention-schedule.md, services/rights.py and the privacy policy all say five years, and the KYC Direction requires identification and address records to be kept at least five years after the business relationship ends. DPDP sets no such minimum and its one-year floor is met, so the early deletion breaches only the sector rule. It applies today.
expected.sector: RBI Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, updated 14 Aug 2025, para 46(b)

expected.issue: Rejected applicants' data is never deleted. The KYC purge joins loans, and the rejected-application delete uses USING loans with l.application_id = a.id, so it matches only applications that became loans, which are never rejected. An applicant with no loan keeps the application, KYC images, selfie, bank statements and contact_graph rows indefinitely, while docs/retention-schedule.md and the privacy policy promise deletion 90 days after the decision. Readiness gap until 13 May 2027.

Each month the job reads the stored account aggregator statements of every active and closed borrower, including those with offers_opt_in false, to set top-up limits. The consent in services/aa_client.py is a one-time fetch with a one-month data life for 'Assess your loan application'. Nothing deletes bank_statements, though docs/retention-schedule.md says jobs/retention.py ends them with the data life, and the privacy policy says offers use repayment history. Readiness gap until 13 May 2027.

When parsing fails, handle_fi_ready logs the whole decrypted account aggregator payload (account holder profile, balances and transactions) at WARNING. deploy/logging.yaml keeps the api-app stream 400 days and lets all of engineering read it. Readiness gap until 13 May 2027.

The live Verilane API key is compiled into the app through buildConfigField. docs/vendors/verilane-api.md says a live key can call every endpoint, including GET /verifications/{reference}, which returns past verifications with their extracted fields and image links, and that references are sequential. Anyone who unpacks the APK can pull every borrower's KYC record. The key value must not be copied into the report. Readiness gap until 13 May 2027.

collections_partner, Recoverline staff on the operations console, can read KYC document images, bank statements and contact_graph for every overdue account from one day past due. The agreement assigns accounts from 60 days past due and Schedule A lists six fields, and the in-house collections role sees only assigned accounts, with no KYC or statement access. Readiness gap until 13 May 2027.

should_not_flag.why: It holds the payment aggregator's token reference, the last four digits, network and expiry, and the e-mandate reference, so it must not be reported as stored card numbers.

The Board row matches s.8(6) and Rule 7 as the catalog states them: intimation without delay, then the detailed report within 72 hours. Who receives the notice to people affected is K1, and the CERT-In row is P5. The RBI row repeats the catalog's 6-hour entry and is not scored either way.

Logs are kept 400 days in ap-south-1 (Mumbai), over the one-year floor in Rule 6(1)(e) and Rule 8(3) and the 180 days in India that CERT-In direction (iv) requires, and the time source follows NPL and NIC as direction (i) requires. Its reader groups matter only for P11.
It texts only the borrower, on the borrower's own number, about their own loan, between 08:00 and 19:00. The messages to third parties are in jobs/collections_escalation.py (P1).

It sends offers only to active borrowers whose offers_opt_in is true at send time, so withdrawal through api/settings.py takes effect on the next run. The gap is offer_scoring.py's use of statements (P10).
Placeholders for local development, not a hardcoded credential.
Addresses on the reserved example.test domain, all-zero phone numbers and X-masked identifiers are plainly synthetic.

One burst of frames at onboarding for liveness, with the camera released afterwards and consent recorded in PermissionsStep.kt. The Directions allow one-time camera access for onboarding or KYC with the borrower's explicit consent (para 12(i)).

Refusing to erase KYC and loan records during their statutory period, with the reason given, is allowed: s.12(3) excepts data whose retention is necessary for the specified purpose or for compliance with any law, and the fintech sector guide says statutory retention overrides erasure. Its five-year statement is right; the purge that breaks it is P8. Refusing data an open loan does not need is K2, and what erase() leaves out is K3.
Grievances are resolved within 30 days, inside the 90-day ceiling in Rule 14(3), and the escalation note matches the 30-day trigger for the RBI Ombudsman in para 11(iv) of the Directions.

Loans go only to residents of India aged 21 to 58 with a PAN and an Indian address, and the README says the company has no establishment, staff or customers outside India. GDPR does not reach it under Art. 3, and no borrower is a child under DPDP s.2(f) and s.9, so GDPR findings and children's findings are out of scope. The required credit_assessment consent covers only what the application needs, and offers are a separate optional consent, off by default.

The policy gives withdrawal, access, correction, erasure, nomination, the grievance officer and the route to the Board, as s.5(1) and Rule 3 require, so none of these may be reported as missing. It itemises the data and purposes except the analytics SDK's screen events (K4). Its unnamed SDK partners are P7, and its statements on references, location, the collections partner and offers are evidence for P1, P2, P3 and P10.

known_gaps.issue: The notice to people affected goes to 'every borrower affected'. Tamarind also holds data of rejected applicants (kept indefinitely, P9), address-book contacts and references (P1) and nominees, and s.8(6) and Rule 7(1) require intimation to each affected Data Principal.

erase() refuses everything while a loan is open, including the non-reference contacts and location history that the notice ties to choosing two references and confirming the city at KYC. An open loan does not need them, so s.12(3) does not excuse keeping them.

When erase() runs, it keeps the nominee, employer, income, AA handle, applications and repayment mandates without listing them in RETAINED, so the borrower is not told they remain, and it sends no erasure instruction to Recoverline, Verilane, Signalgrid or Pulsemetric.

docs/vendors/register.md says Pulsemetric collects screen events and android/app/build.gradle calls it screen analytics, but the policy's data table lists only device model, identifiers, IP address and network type.

Only the offers consent can be withdrawn. PermissionsStep.kt records a consent for each permission, but nothing withdraws them, and revoking the Android permission leaves the stored contact graph and locations in use, though the policy promises withdrawal of any consent in the app.

Nothing handles account aggregator consent revocation or expiry. aa_consents.status is set to requested and then active, never to revoked or expired, so a revoked consent does not stop use of the stored statements.

The SMS gateway's entry gives a services agreement with no processing terms, unlike every other vendor, and the payment aggregator behind repayment_mandates.pa_token_ref is not in the register. The contracts are not in the material, so this is 'not found in the reviewed material', medium at most.
export() leaves out preapproved_offers, which erase() deletes.

sources.claim: Digital Lending Directions: para 3 applies to all NBFCs; para 4(v) defines a lending service provider to include recovery; para 11(iv) lets a borrower go to the RBI Ombudsman with no reply in 30 days; para 12(i) requires need-based collection with prior explicit consent and an audit trail, bars access to file and media, contact list, call logs and telephony functions, and allows one-time camera, microphone or location access for onboarding or KYC only; para 13(i) limits service providers to basic data; para 13(iv) requires storage only in India, with data processed abroad deleted there and brought back within 24 hours; para 14(ii) requires the privacy policy to disclose third parties collecting through the app.
sources.source: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, RBI/2025-26/36, 8 May 2025, https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12848, read 11 Nov 2026. /dpdp-catalog has the instrument and paras 12-14.

sources.claim: CERT-In: direction (i) syncs clocks to NIC or NPL; direction (ii) reports incidents within 6 hours of noticing or being told; direction (iv) keeps ICT logs 180 days within Indian jurisdiction. FAQ 24 starts the clock at noticing; FAQ 25 makes any company a body corporate; FAQ 30 allows a partial first report and lists data breaches and leaks; FAQ 35 lets logs sit outside India if produced in reasonable time, so log location is not planted.
sources.source: https://www.cert-in.org.in/PDF/CERT-In_Directions_70B_28.04.2022.pdf and https://www.cert-in.org.in/PDF/FAQs_on_CyberSecurityDirections_May2022.pdf, text extracted 11 Nov 2026. /dpdp-catalog has the 6-hour and 180-day rows.

sources.claim: KYC Direction: para 3(b)(xiv) covers NBFCs; para 16, Explanation 1, makes the lender ensure the customer redacts or blacks out the Aadhaar number where authentication is not required; para 46(b) keeps identification and address records at least five years after the business relationship ends.
sources.source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, updated 14 Aug 2025, https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=11566, read 11 Nov 2026. The fintech sector guide's 'KYC records: 5 years after business relationship ends' agrees.

sources.claim: DPDP sections and rules, commencement and the absence of a restricted country under s.16.
sources.source: /dpdp-catalog, last verified 2 Nov 2026. The wording of s.2(f) (a child has not completed eighteen years), s.12(3) (erase on request unless retention is necessary for the specified purpose or for compliance with any law) and s.16 (the Central Government may restrict transfers by notification; s.16(2) keeps in force any law giving higher protection or restricting transfers) was checked on 11 Nov 2026 against the Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II Section 1, No. 25, 11 Aug 2023, https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/248045.pdf.
Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Art. 3, on EUR-Lex. /gdpr-catalog has no Art. 3 row.

unverified: Sector guide and /dpdp-catalog: 6-hour reporting to RBI under the RBI Cybersecurity Directions, 2026. Not opened, so the key does not score the runbook's RBI row.

Sector guide: payment system data must be stored in India under the 2018 RBI circular, 'reinforced 2024'. The circular was not opened and the 2024 reinforcement was not traced. The key relies on para 13(iv) of the Digital Lending Directions instead.
Sector guide: 'Transaction records: 10 years (RBI for banks)'. Not traced. Para 46(a) of the KYC Direction says five years from the transaction. Not used.
Sector guide: 'Aadhaar Act restrictions apply; never store Aadhaar number in plain text'. The Aadhaar Act was not checked. The key relies on para 16 of the KYC Direction.

Card-on-file limits for merchants: the RBI tokenisation circulars were not found. The Payment Aggregator Master Direction of 15 Sep 2025, Annexure-1 clause 2.1, keeps card credentials off servers the merchant accesses. The key makes no card-storage claim; the repayment_mandates item rests on the table's columns.
PMLA s.12 record-keeping: not opened. The key cites the KYC Direction only.
